facts.text: Coffman Cove began as a logging camp in the 1950s, laying the groundwork for the community that would later become a city.
The town officially incorporated as a city in 1989, marking its transition from a small logging settlement to a recognized municipality.
Coffman Cove sits along the Inside Passage on the east side of Prince of Wales Island, a key maritime corridor in Southeast Alaska.
The area is a temperate rainforest, receiving high precipitation and enjoying mild summers while experiencing cold winters typical of the region.
Scheduled float‑plane service, including flights by Taquan Air, connects Coffman Cove to other island communities and mainland destinations.
Ferry service to Coffman Cove was suspended in 2009, but by 2020 the Alaska Marine Hi‑way restored connections from Bellingham and Prince Rupert via Ketchikan.
